. The higher level of geopolitical competition and remilitarization, even without military conflict, has its costs, both for the region itself and for the planet as a whole. The nearly half-century-long Cold War led to an unprecedented level of militarization in the Arctic, with many damaging impacts, including toxins, debris, and abandoned infrastructure across the tundra, which polluted environments and damaged Indigenous homelands. Militarization comes at a severe cost for the human security of the people who call the Arctic their home. The argument is often made that the foremost national security threat for all countries is that of climate change.
